articleTitle: Linear SVM classifier based HOG car detection
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Improving safety and reducing accidents are the most goals of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). For their low cost and capability of providing information about driving environments, Vision-based driver assistance systems are the most important systems in recent years. In these systems, robust and precise vehicle detection is a critical step, and the detected cars can be used for various applications. This paper presents an algorithm for vehicle detection in an urban environment which is very important for driver assistance systems and autonomous driving. To succeed the detection of a vehicle, we propose the histogram of oriented gradients features descriptor (HOG) and linear support vector machine (SVM) for the classification. Our experimental results illustrate the robustness and precision of our algorithm for different scenes.

Author Keywords: histogram of oriented gradients features descriptor

articleTitle: Fusion of ANN and SVM classifiers for network attack detection
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: With the progressive increase of network application and electronic devices (computer, mobile phones, android, etc), attack and intrusion detection is becoming a very challenging task in cybercrime detection area. In this context, most of existing approaches of attack detection rely mainly on a finite set of attacks. However, these solutions are vulnerable, that is, they fail in detecting some attacks when sources of informations are ambiguous or imperfect. But, few approaches started investigating toward this direction. Following this trends, this paper investigates the role of machine learning approach (ANN, SVM)in detecting TCP connection traffic as normal or suspicious one. But, using ANN and SVM is an expensive technique individually. In this paper, combining two classifiers has been proposed, where artificial neural network (ANN) classifier and support vector machine (SVM) were employed. Additionally, our proposed solution allows to visualize obtained classification results. Accuracy of the proposed solution has been compared with other classifier results. Experiments have been conducted with different network connection selected from NSL-KDD DARPA dataset. Empirical results show that combining ANN and SVM techniques for attack detection is a promising direction.

articleTitle: Control of five-phase PMSM for electric vehicle application
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The increasing need of reliability and high efficiency of the electric vehicles makes the multi-phase electric machines very attractive and highly recommended in transport applications. This paper investigates the vector control strategy of multi-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine under different drive cycles. Thus, the dynamic model of the electric vehicle is presented and a variable speed control is applied under variable load conditions. The simulations are carried out under MATLAB© \ Simulink © environment and the obtained results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Impact of dust accumulation on PV panel performance in the Saharan region
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this work, we present modeling the dust effect on the monocrystalline silicon Photovoltaic Panel (Sharp NT-R5E3E175W) in Saharan region (Adrar, Algeria) the model can be used to develop a simulation program. Its principle is based on the self-consistent iterative numerical solution of the Poisson and continuity and the transport equations. The discretization method used is that of finite differences. The parameters characterizing the solar cell such as short-circuit current, open-circuit voltage, fill factor, efficiency will be deducted from the simulated current-voltage characteristics. To validate the effectiveness of this numerical model, we will compare the simulation results with experimental measurements. Sufficient agreement was observed when we compared the experimental results of the photovoltaic panel.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic controller for autonomous vehicle path tracking
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work deals with the problem of path tracking for an electric vehicle which has four electromechanical wheel Systems. A controller based on fuzzy logic sends the speed and the steering instructions to the robot to ensure that the robot follows the trajectory, during the design of this controller the effort was concentrated on the simplicity and efficiency. The processing and response time are very essential factors in the process control, which is what motivated the choices of the structure and the parameters of the different parts of the fuzzy controller. The effectiveness of the proposed trajectory control method are confirmed by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Impact of partial shading and PV array power on the performance of grid connected PV station
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this article, we present the study of the partial shading influence, and the effect of different PV array power on grid-connected photovoltaic stations performance mounted in the desert region of Algeria at the end of the year 2016. To evaluate these effects on PV central performance. we analyzed the measured data, which are derived from monitoring of climate parameters (solar irradiation, ambient temperature) and other electrical parameters (power, energy) during a clear day such as a monitoring period. The analysis of the experimental data shows that the partial shading can be influence on DC/AC output power and DC/AC energy of the grid connected PV system, then it affects the performance parameter such as the efficiencies (PV, inverter and system) of power and energy, the yields (array and final) and the performance ration. While the PV array power that influence on the inverter efficiency, because of the efficacy of maximum power point tracking technique for PV inverter, which is depend of the level DC input power.

articleTitle: Design of patch array antennas for future 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to investigate the design of rectangular patch antenna arrays fed by miscrostrip and coaxial lines at 28 GHz for future 5G applications. Our objective is to design a four element antenna array with a bandwidth higher than 1 GHz and a maximum radiation gain. The performances of the rectangular 4*1 and 2*2 patch antenna arrays designed on Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate were optimized and the simulation results reveal that the performance of 4*1 antenna array fed by microstrip line is better than 2*2 antenna array fed by coaxial cable. We obtained for the topology of 4*1 rectangular patch array antenna a bandwidth of 2.15 GHz and 1.3 GHz respectively with almost similar gains of the order of 13.3 dBi.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of RPL objective functions for multi-sink
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: RPL (Routing Protocol for Low Power and Lossy networks) is a routing protocol for Low power and Lossy networks (LLN) in the internet of thing, standardized by Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). RPL is a distance-vector protocol. It constructs an acyclic graph called DODAG (Destination Oriented Directed Acyclic Graph), allowing to establish the routes towards the sink. DODAG overns the route depending on certain metrics injected into objective function. This paper presents an evaluation of RPL performance, using the Cooja simulator, while increasing the sinks number in the network. This modification affects the RPL performance: lost packet and energy consumption are reduced, on the other hand; PDR, received packet and throughput are increased.

articleTitle: An MR brain images classification technique via the Gaussian radial basis kernel and SVM
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) and artificial intelligence (AI) are hot topics in the field of clinical imaging and neuro-imaging. Recently numerous methods were proposed. In this research work, a new 3D magnetic resonance head images (MRI) classifier based on KPCA and SVM is presented. The proposed algorithm, called the support vector machine with kernel principal component analysis (SVM-KPCA), aims to classify an MR brain image as normal or pathological. The system first employed the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to extract features from the images. After feature vector normalization the kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) is applied to reduce the dimensionality of features. The reduced features were then submitted to a support vector machine (SVM). The strategy of k-fold cross-validation was used to enhance generalization of the proposed algorithm. Seven common brain diseases have been used (Alzheimer's disease, Alzheimer's disease plus visual agnosia, glioma, meningioma, Huntington's disease, sarcoma and Pick's disease) as pathological brains, and MR brain images have been collected from `Harvard Medical School' website and `Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS)' website, to validate the proposed algorithm. Simulation results were compared with the existing algorithms and it was observed that the proposed work outperforms other algorithms. Working on the same dataset in term of accuracy, sensitivity and specificity.

articleTitle: A simple filtered high gain observer for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: A high gain observer involving a linear filter is proposed. The structure of the proposed Filtered High Gain Observer (FHGO) is very simple and consists in two cascaded systems having the same dimension as the original system. The first subsystem is a copy of the original system with a simple correction term which only (linearly) depends on the state of the second subsystem. The latter is a linear filter which input is the output observation error, i.e. the error between the output measurement and its value predicted by the first subsystem. The design of the FHGO is first carried out by assuming that the outputs are available in a continuous manner. Then, a redesigned version is proposed in order to account for the sampling process of the output. Simulation results dealing with a forced Van Der Pol oscillator are given for illustration purposes.

articleTitle: Control of relative humidity inside an agricultural greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The development of intelligent systems in agriculture is required to improve plant production. The first part of this paper is a general study of the greenhouse and its climatic factors essential for the growth of the plant. In the second part, two controls have been adjusted to assimilate the humidity control; the PID controller and the fuzzy logic controller.

articleTitle: MPPT controllers for PV array panel connected to Grid
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper proposes a grid-connected Photovoltaic energy system through a three-phases DC-AC converter. For this purpose, the characterization of the PV system, integrating the maximum power point strategy (MPPT) based on Fractional Open-Circuit Voltage (FOV) and Fractional Short-Circuit Current (FSC) methods, is developed and treated under the software MATLAB / Simulink. Thereafter, the proposed design of three phases grid-connected inverter system has been simulated.

articleTitle: Optimal appliances scheduling for demand response strategy in smart home
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Demand response programs play potential roles in improving the performance and the reliability in smart homes as well as in reducing peak demand and increasing the energy efficiency in residential sector. The aim of this study is to propose an optimal household energy management for residential consumers. In this context, a “Demand response strategy for home power management” is developed. This proposed strategy is built to minimize peak demand by scheduling the appliances operation and moving the shiftable loads during peak periods, when hourly electricity prices are high, to off-peak hours especially when prices are low without affecting the customers' comfort live, ensuring therefore a flatten power load curve. The system results are simulated by using MATLAB software in order to prove the efficiency of the proposed supervision strategy to control the daily household energy consumption.

articleTitle: Nonlinear control of a permanent magnet synchronous generator in wind energy conversion system with maximum power extraction
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: A nonlinear control of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) in Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) with maximum power extraction is presented. The control strategy is guaranteed in two steps. In the first step, different MPPT techniques are designed to track the maximum power point (MPP). Four MPPT techniques, in order to guarantee the maximum wind power, are presented which are: Tip Speed Ratio (TSR) method, Optimal Torque Control (OTC) method, Perturb and Observe (P&O) method and Modified Enhanced Perturb and Observe (MEPO). Whereas in the second step, a Sliding Mode Control (SMC) is applied to control the PMSG in variable speed WECS. The SMC has many advantages such as simplicity against parameter uncertainties. The WECS is developed in MATLAB/SIMULINK. The performance of MPPT techniques and SMC controller are validated via simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the QoS parameters in different SDN architecture using Omnet 4.6++
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The main Specification of the quality of service (QoS) is that the signaling must be capable of carrying out traffic characteristics such as bandwidth and QoS are needed. This paper presents the performance evaluation of QoS parameters such as gigue, latency, lost packets, end-to-end delay, MOS under Omnet 4.6++ for all types of Software Defined Networking (SDN) topologies “Hierarchical, star, ring, tree”, in order to determine the architecture most suitable for the latter, via the implementation and simulation of the OpenFlow protocol.

articleTitle: PSpice and Simulink co-simulation for diode and AC-DC converter using SLPS interface software
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, a high efficiency AC-DC converter has been analysed based on co-simulation of PSpice simulator and Simulink using the SLPS interface program. An enhanced electro thermal model of power diode has been developed. The diode was implemented in the Pspice circuit simulation platform using Pspice standard components and analog behavior modeling (ABM) blocks. Potentially, the suggested model is able to trace the electrical effects. This model was confirmed through a comparison with other models having close characteristics for different circuits (DC-DC converter, turn-on and turn-off). It is first realized in PSpice software and integrated in Simulink via SLPS software. In a second step, the converter is simulated using MATLAB-Simulink.

articleTitle: Optimal trajectory generation and flatness tracking control for a mobile robot
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work proposes an optimal trajectory generation and a controller design for a mobile robot. The objective consists of creating a new performance guidance module for the mobile robot in a closed environment. The reference trajectory can be calculated by solving an optimization problem. The properties of the differential flatness, the B-spline and the direct collocation method are exploited to convert the constrained optimization problem into a nonlinear programming one that can be easily resolved by a classic solver. After that, the obtained optimal reference trajectory is used in the kinematic mobile robot model. A flatness-based controller is designed to ensure the trajectory tracking. The numerical simulations are done in order to evaluate the proposed optimal trajectory generation approach and the tracking strategy.

articleTitle: Sizing optimization of a stand-alone photovoltaic system using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The Stand-Alone Photovoltaic (SAPV) system's power reliability and the corresponding Life Cycle Cost (LCC) present the main designing objectives. Therefore, a compromise solution between optimization criterions is crucial. This paper presents the sizing optimization of a stand-alone photovoltaic system with battery storage using Genetic Algorithm (GA). The main objective is computing the optimum configuration of the PV panels and storage batteries to supply a residential household. The purpose is to achieve an acceptable Loss of Power Supply Probability (LPSP), which is related to system's reliability, and the minimum LCC. The system's performance evaluation for different configurations of PV panels and batteries for a two-day simulation with an hourly step time was done. It was based on energetic modeling of the studied SAPV system. Sizing optimization insured consumers supply, a minimum LCC and an acceptable batteries State Of Charge (SOC).

articleTitle: Modelling and control of greenhouses powered by a renewable energy system
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The control of greenhouses consists of regulating different parameters such as temperature, humidity, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> concentration in the air, etc. This work is based on the study of the optimal environmental conditions for growing tomatoes when the sources of energy are renewable (photovoltaic and wind). So, to regulate the heating and ventilation inside the greenhouse, we integrated a wind-PV hybrid generation system. In fact, our work focuses on the modelling, simulation and analysis of such systems in a MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Hardware implementation of 1-D 8-point adaptive multiple transform in post-HEVC standard
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Despite the coding efficiency improvement cognized per HEVC standard, researchers are still devoting so much efforts for further enhancements. The latest result of ITU-T and ISO/IEC collaboration was the definition of a new standardization initiative beyond HEVC which is POST-HEVC standard. It is actually under development and scheduled to be completed in 2020. It offers many contributions specifically in the transform module. In fact, it has introduced a new approach called Adaptive Multiple Transform (AMT) which raises the issue of additional computational complexity. This work proposes hardware architectures of the 1-D 8-point Adaptive Multiple Transform for all transform types. This theme is innovative since it was not dealt with before. In this paper two transform implementations aspects are detailed and compared. The first method is based on using Altera multipliers (LPM) and the second one exploits correlation and symmetry properties in order to reduce matrix multiplications complexity. The adopted method was implemented in VHDL and it is capable to process at 288 MHZ under a Stratix III device. The number of execution cycles of this architecture can reach a maximum of 12 cycles when 8-point-1D-DCT-VIII is computed.

articleTitle: Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm for the high gain observer optimization. Application to chaos synchronization
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The problem posed by this paper is the state synchronization of nonlinear perturbed chaotic systems by employing an optimal high gain observer, which optimization is derived by the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). Such a procedure is proved to be an efficient multiobjective search technique in various applications. Thus, a new quadratic optimization criterion is proposed to calculate the required optimal value of the observer setting parameter θ that characterizes the observation gain. The adopted fitness function allows achieving a compromise between the observation error and the correction term of the high gain observer. Moreover, the stability of this designed approach is studied using the Lyapunov framework. Simulations are proposed to prove the efficiency of the proposed synchronization scheme on the well-known unified perturbed chaotic system.

articleTitle: Applications to function approximation and system control based on wavelet networks
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In the framework of nonlinear process modeling, we present conventional wavelet neural network used as nonlinear dynamic models type simple pendulum, this architecture is tuned by gradient-based techniques. Initialization procedure of wavelet coefficients will be established by the heuristic method. Performances of the initiated approach have been emphasized by results obtained from several experiences.

articleTitle: Low voltage low power current comparator circuit
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents a high speed, low voltage, low power current comparator. A modification to an existing current comparator proposed by Traff has been introduced. The circuit presents a two flipped voltage follower current mirrors (FVF) connected in parallel which replaces the input stage of the existing current comparator of Tang and Pun. This modification allows us to reach the higher speed, lower voltage and lower power dissipation. ELDO simulators using 0.18 μm, CMOS and TSMC parameters are performed to confirm the workability of this circuit. The proposed current comparator circuit is powered with a 1 V supply voltage. It is characterized by wide conversion frequency 2 GHz and a low power consumption that is about 0.208 mW.

articleTitle: Improvement of energy management algorithm for fuel cell electrical vehicle with fuzzy logic
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: To meet increasing demands for fuel, alternative vehicles have been developed recently. Electrical hybrid vehicles are one of these alternatives and an important part of them is their energy storage systems which are used to relieve the main source which is generally a fuel cell. To ensure energy storage, the supercapacitor is considered as an interesting device because of its high power density compared to batteries. The hybridization of the main source with another source like energy storage device allows to improve the dynamic response, especially, during transient states. However, it will be necessary to apply an energy management strategy to share the energy flow between sources responding to load demand. Besides, the proposed energy management algorithm must allow us to ensure optimum hydrogen consumption. In this context, this paper deals with two energy management strategies, the first is based on some rules, the second is based on fuzzy logic. Simulation results under Matlab-Simulink environment prove the efficiency of the proposed strategies.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis and accommodation for singularly perturbed time-delayed systems: Descriptor approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work deals with the fault diagnosis and fault tolerant control for singularly perturbed time-delayed systems against sensor failures. The estimation of sensor faults is based on the descriptor approach which introduce the faults in the system having the property of auxiliary state. So, we construct an observer based on this approach and we use the technique of ε-dependent Linear Matrix Inequalities(LMI) in order to determine the observer gains. Then, an output-feedback controller gain is calculated to stabilize the system in both the fault free case and the faulty case. Finally, a numerical example with various form of sensor faults is presented.

articleTitle: Real time implementation of perturb and observe algorithm and PI controller for DC/DC converter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work presents an approach to the design of a medium power boost converter (less than 300 W) dedicated to photovoltaic systems. The converter is designed to adapt the voltage of the solar panel to a stable voltage output to recharge a batteries. The control of the converter is of the digital type, using a ATMEGA microcontroller. Two control algorithms are studied in this paper: The first uses two control loops which are the voltage and current supplied by the photovoltaic panel (PV), an image of the input power Pe. This algorithm is designed to follow the point at Maximum power point(MPPT) of the characteristic P (V) of the panel. The second is a PI regulator designed to set the output voltage at 48V.

articleTitle: A 5.2 GHz high gain high isolation double balance Gilbert cell mixer with linearity improvement in TSMC 180nm CMOS technology for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents a high gain, high isolation double balance (DB) Gilbert cell mixer, designed in 180nm RF CMOS process, is proposed to be suitable for WLAN communication systems at 5.2 GHZ frequency. The proposed folded Gilbert mixer employs an inductive degeneration source and a differential trans-conductance to set the better trend between linearity, port isolation, gain and noise. Simulation results reveal that at operating frequency 5.2 GHZ, the proposed mixer furnishes 9.48 dB of conversion gain and minimum value of noise figure of 8.6 dB. The 1-db compression point is 4 dBm and the LO-RF, LO-IF and RF-IF isolations are 83 dB, 80 dB and 103 dB, respectively, which ensure the enhanced port-to-port isolations and improved linearity criterion.

articleTitle: Multisensor data fusion for electrical wheelchair localization using extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The number of wheelchair users have been increased. In this paper, the wheelchair localization problem is studied. To localize the electrical wheelchair a sensor information is needed. This paper presents a data fusion technique which combine data from multiple sensor. The objective of this paper is to localize the electrical wheelchair in indoor environment using Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm and ultrasonic sensors with wheeled encoders. Also, a kinematic model of the robot is determined. The proposed method is successfully tested in simulation.

articleTitle: Synergetic control for three-tanks system: A comparison with the sliding mode control
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the chattering problem of sliding mode control (SMC). Firstly, the SMC is introduced. The synergetic control is also can be a solution to alleviate chattering problem. The synergetic theory will be presented. The connection between SMC and the proposed control will be developed. Moreover we will apply the two approaches for Multiple-Inputs Multiple-Outputs (MIMO). Common elements and main differences between SMC and synergetic control are proved through a comparative simulation results using the three-tank system.

articleTitle: Observer-based control for a class of polynomial systems with time delay
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of observer-based control for a class of polynomial systems. A polynomial observer to estimate unmeasurable states of polynomial systems is proposed. For the analysis of the global asymptotic stability, a design method is proposed. In this approach we adopt a polynomial Lyapunov krasovskii function with designed polynomial Lyapunov matrix. The design conditions in the proposed approach are represented in terms of Sum Of Squares (SOS) which can be numerically and symbolically solved via the recent developed SOSTOOLS and a Semi-Definite Program (SDP) solver. Finally, two numerical examples are introduced to show the validity and applicability of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Cascade temperature control of an automotive turbocharger hot-gas test-stand
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: An experimental implementation of cascade control on the turbine inlet temperature of a turbocharger turbine is presented. The experimental setup used was a hot gas test stand developed for the determination of compressor and turbine characteristic maps of automotive turbochargers. The cascade control consisted of turbine inlet temperature as the outer loop (primary controller), while the propane buffer tank pressure feeding the burner as the inner loop (secondary controller). The propane buffer tank pressure was controlled through pulse width modulation of a solenoid valve connected to a propane cylinder. Temperature control between 500°C and 800°C (which is indicative of engine exhaust temperature) is presented along with the propane pressure control traces. The effect of the propane buffer tank size (which translates to the response time of the inner loop) is discussed. Also discussed is the inclusion of a propane orifice just upstream of the burner to match the increase/decrease rates of propane pressure in the buffer tank. This matching of pressure increase/decrease rates helped in simplifying the control scheme and removed the need for gain scheduling.

articleTitle: A fault tolerant control for robot manipulators against actuator fault
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper considers the control problem for the robot manipulator systems affected by an actuator fault. The dynamic model of the robot manipulator is presented taking into account several physical phenomena, which can influence the dynamics of the system. Subsequently, two control schemes (FTC) for the faulty system are developed, one based on the sliding mode approach, while the second approach (backstepping) is based on the Lyapunov theorem. In the last part, an adaptive observer is made to estimate this fault. The simulation results showed the efficiency of the control methods calculated based on the nonlinear model to tolerate the presence of an actuator faults, as well as the efficience of the estimator.

articleTitle: Optimal sliding mode control for a class of uncertain discrete-time systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper proposes a Discrete Optimal Sliding Mode Control (D-OSMC) algorithm for uncertain linear systems. The parameter uncertainties are assumed to be unknown but norm-bounded. Firstly, for the nominal system, an optimal control law is derived to satisfy linear quadratic performance index. To overcome the problem accompanying the choice of the matrix of the matrix of the sliding surface, a novel method based on the resolution of a Sylvester equation is proposed. In order to ensure the robustness of the system during the reaching phase, a novel optimal discrete integral, sliding surface is designed. Simulation results have been presented to confirm the usefulness and the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: MPPT algorithm for wind energy conversion system based on PMSG
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper deals with wind energy conversion system (WECS). The system includes essentially wind turbine, permanent magnetic synchronous generator and power converters. All these parts have been modeled. In addition a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) method is presented. We have been used a specific controller to maintain a constant level voltage at the DC bus. An LCL type filter has been used to obtain a perfect sinusoidal signal, after the inverter. Although, we have been present a control of active and reactive power. All the parts of system have been simulated on Matlab-Simulink software and the results are presented at the end of paper.

articleTitle: Design of high performance and low power dissipation operational transconductance amplifier by using MATLAB optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI), Operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) become one of the most significant building blocks of analog circuit. The optimized of calculation transistor dimensions of the Miller OTA by using MATLAB code plays an important parameter to have higher performance and low power than a manual calculator. This paper presents a low power OTA based on OTA Miller, which operates at 1.8V power supply voltage. The proposed OTA exhibit DC gain of 68 dB, and gain bandwidth of 15.27 MHz with 0.243 mW power dissipation. The Phase Margin (PM) and slew rate of the proposed OTA are 71.97° and 21.5 V/μs respectively. Design and simulation have been carried by T-Spice using TSMC 0.18um CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Suspicious behavior detection based on DECOC classifier
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Video surveillance systems become quickly an essential criteria and requirement for safety systems. The traditional systems based on manual vision should be replaced by intelligent decision. These systems suffer from not only lack of confidence but also from the worst accuracy. Many intelligent systems are proposed in literature to ensure automation and intelligent decision. Suspicious behavior as a particular case of surveillance, presents a great challenge. Problems faced of researchers are the difficulty of the behavior's detection and the real-time processing. This paper is focused in an abnormal behavior detection. A suspicious behavior recognition is proposed using Data-driven Error Correcting Output Code (DECOC) classifier. The proposed is proved in the experiment section in comparison with the most recent approaches.

articleTitle: Stability bound analysis of slow sampling discrete-time singularly perturbed systems with time-delay
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper treats the stability bound problem of discrete linear singularly perturbed system (SPSs) with time delay is treated. Using an appropriate Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, satisfactory conditions formulated in terme of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs) are proposed to analyse the asymptotic stability of SPSs. Delay independent and delay dependent stability criterion are treated. Illustrative examples are provided to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Orthotopic approach of set-membership parameters estimation for LPV system using fractional models
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method of set membership identification for linear parameter varying (LPV) fractional system is presented, where the probability distribution of the disturbances is assumed unknown but bounded. In such context, the new approach consists of enclosing all feasible parameters by an outer orthotope. The performance of the new approach has been evaluated using a numerical example and a Monte Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: Low-voltage low-power four-quadrant analog multiplier in current-mode
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, a four-quadrant multiplier designed by squarer circuit and rectifier is presented. The circuit is evaluated using ELDO simulator in 0.18μm CMOS parameters. For input range of ±20μA and a power supply voltage of ±0.6V, the THD, the -3db bandwidth and the power consumption are 0.75%, 32.2MHz and 0.63mW, respectively.

articleTitle: New approach and layers designs of sharing energy system for interconnected microgrid
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In SMART Grid concept, many works talk about energy management and its benefits to save and control energy in any electrical grid application. However, the “management” term is very large to focus and study some particular case. So, this paper introduces a new concept focusing closely on “Sharing energy” in multi-sources and multi-consumers case with variable parameters. Our approach is developed around a new “protocol stack model” made by two levels: physical and algorithmic layers. By using a modified “demand side management algorithm”, we propose in this paper a simulation example of an energy sharing algorithm that allows users to plan the daily consumption of their households by respecting a variable price tariff of the public company of electricity and the residual energy in photovoltaic system accumulator. The main goal is to reduce the total cost and the peak-to-average ratio.

articleTitle: Induction machine faults diagnosis by statistical neural networks with selection variables based on Principal component analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The early diagnosis of induction machine faults has become an exigency in all industrial process, as it reduces the breakdowns occurrence. Therefore, the importance of motor defect detection and their classification has recently result numerous research studies on the application of artificial neural network. In this paper, an effectual radial basis function neural networks (RBFN) and probabilistic neural networks (PNN) based method with dimensionality diminution is suggested for online motor current signal analysis. In order to minimize huge databases, Principal Component analysis is developed for selecting convenient training parameters. The classification performance comparison of RBFN and PNN is applied for the proposed method.

articleTitle: A data-driven approach based health indicator for remaining useful life estimation of bearings
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Accurate state of health monitoring remains an important challenge in the modern industry. Failures in rolling element bearings account for almost half of all machine breakdowns. Consequently, the monitoring of this component is very required for arranging repair work and reducing unexpected production outage. In this sense, this paper presents a new data-driven approach for bearing remaining useful life estimation. Considering the nonlinear and non-stationary bearing vibration signals, the empirical mode decomposition method was used as a pre-processing step for feature extraction. Then, the principal component analysis algorithm was used for feature reduction. Finally, the support vector regression algorithm is proposed to estimate the remaining useful life of the tested bearing. In fact, the proposed method presents a new health indicator that defines accurately the state of health of bearings. Experimental results based on real bearing vibration signals under real operating conditions confirm the reliability and the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study and simulation of three-phase seven-level packed U cells inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Since 2008, the Packed U Cells (PUC) converter has been presented as a new topology of multilevel converter with a very high energy efficiency potential compared to the old topologies. In this paper, a three-phase PUC inverter has been proposed. A voltage balancing controller is designed to apply the seven levels of the inverter; this is done by regulate the output voltage of the DC capacitors to a desired value in order to obtain seven levels at the output of the inverter. Pulse width modulation technique is used to generate the associated pulses to control the switches of the converter. In order to test the performances of the proposed controller the behaviour of this later is simulated under Matlab-Simulink for a variable load. The results obtained have shown a fast and efficient response under different conditions.

articleTitle: Delay-dependent H∞ controller design for discrete Switched system: An average dwell time approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This study involves problem of state feedback controller (SFC) design for switched systems with time varying delay. The essential objective is to create a state feedback controller with a switching rule assuring the robust exponential stability and guarantee an H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> performance of the resulting closed loop hybrid system. Applying Average Dwell Time (ADT) approaches and using appropriate Lyapunov Krasovskii functional (LKf), LMI-based criterion is developed to deal with problem H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> analysis and synthesis. Simulation examples including the comparisons are relevant to expose the merit of the designed technique.

articleTitle: Navigation and trajectory tracking of mobile robot based on kinematic PI controller
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In last few years there has been a growing interest in trajectory tracking and mobile robot navigation. In this paper, an effective design of a PI (Proportional Integral) controller to resolve two tasks ‘going to target’ and ‘following a trajectory’ is developed. This controller is designed to adjust the motor velocities of our considered platform (Khepera II). The responses of the robot controller in navigation and tracking have been obtained and graphically presented. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is discussed.

articleTitle: Closed loop for regulation of AC voltages of cascaded PV generator-boost converter-five levels NPC inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Recent developments in power electronics and control methods have produced photovoltaic based DC to AC converters related to AC load. Cascaded boost converter and inverter find their way in interconnecting PV and load. This paper deals with digital simulation of closed loop controlled five levels inverter based photovoltaic system. The objectives of this work are to stabilise the output voltage and reduce the harmonics using all inverter voltage vectors. The maximum power point tracking based on the “perturb & observe” (P&O) approach as a control strategy of a boost DC-DC converter is applied. To maintain the four capacitors voltages of DC bus equal, the redundant vectors of space vector diagram of five levels inverter are used. Without any system to regulate the fluctuation of the DC bus and to get a stable output inverter voltage, authors in this paper propose a proportional regulator of inverter modulation index. Design procedure and control strategy of system are presented in detail. A complete simulation with different profiles of irradiance is presented to prove the excellent performance of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: FPGA-based implementation of TZsearch algorithm for H.265/HEVC standard
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: There are several standard techniques that have emerged within the framework of international video coding standards. The newest and most efficient is the H.265 / HEVC. However, its techniques possess a degree of complexity which remains increasingly high and generate consequently a long computation time, in particular the technique of motion estimation. This operation is largely involved in compression by eliminating temporal redundancies and it is the most sensitive part in a video encoder. As a result, algorithmic optimizations are required to reduce the complexity and computational time. We are interested in the most efficient algorithm for motion estimation which is the “TZ search”. In fact, this work aims to implement an optimized fast search algorithm that maintains the good performance of the process. So, it proposes hardware architecture of fast motion estimation algorithm for H.265/HEVC standard using Test Zone Search (TZS). It presents pipeline processing techniques, minimum latency and maximum bite rate. The proposed VHDL code has been tested through Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA circuit. The frequency result is estimated at 197 Mhz.

articleTitle: Synthesis of decentralized optimal control of nonlinear interconnected systems with block pulse functions application to a double-parallel inverted pendulum
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper deals with synthesis of decentralized optimal control law of nonlinear interconnected systems using a direct approach. The block pulse functions (BPFs) is rigorously developed to solve problems. This tool transforms the optimal control problem to a nonlinear programming problem. Effectiveness of the method is checked through on an interconnected double-parallel inverted pendulum.

articleTitle: Modeling of a single-phase grid-connected photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: To be able to function in connected or islanded mode, microgrid must be robust in synchronization with the network. This paper presents a model of a residential microgrid with three houses with connection with the electrical communication and the possibility feed of storing energy in batteries and the reinforcement of security system. To maximize the energy production one integrates regulators MPPT (Maximum Power Point Alignment) have an advanced technology, which searches permanently the point of maximum capacity, which makes it possible to draw the best performances from the photovoltaic panels. In this paper, we will present a microgrid connected with the single-phase network, to control the inverter we have to replace the PI regulator by a regulator PR (controller resonant) that will increase the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on automotive valve jump/bounce detection: Through use of knock sensor and energy comparison
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper details the experimental work performed on the verification of the dynamic kinematic performance of camshafts designed and fabricated for operation on a turbocharged Kawaski 600cc spark ignition engine. The engine can operate to 12500rpm and the camshafts were shown to incur jump/bounce at speeds higher than 12500 rpm as designed. The Original Equipment Manufacturer OEM naturally aspirated 600cc engine was turbocharged for Formula SAE competition which gave the motivation to design bespoke camshafts suited for the introduction of the turbocharger in the flow stream. Cam valve timings and lobe profiles for the intake and exhaust valves were designed using Ricardo Wave and Valdyn. The purposely built test stand is detailed together with the sensing and data analysis performed for jump/bounce detection. A commercial knock sensor mounted on the cylinder head together with data analysis in LabView were used.

articleTitle: 3D Gabor-Edge filters applied to face depth images
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This manuscript introduces a novel 3D face authentication system inspired from the advantageous capacities of Gabor-Edge filters. The approach studies 3D face difficulties such as expression variety, different rotations and exposure to illuminations. The proposed systems starts by preprocessing the 3D face images to resolve acquisition problems. Then, a filtering process is performed by implanting our 3D Gabor-Edge technique extended based on the classic 3D Gabor masks. The next step is to achieve the classification of facial features from the edge saliency by the artificial Neural Network Classifier (NNC). The evaluation of the adopted system is achieved by exporting common datasets from GavabDB database. Experimental results are reported to prove the high accuracy rates of our method compared to the recent researches in the same biometric field.

articleTitle: Simultaneous state and fault estimation for linear stochastic systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the simultaneous robust state and fault estimation problem for uncertain systems subject to uncertainties. Robust recursive least-squares estimation approach is considered in this study. The paper proposes robust and optimal filters that enforce a minimum state-error variance property for any allowed uncertainties. The unknown additive fault affects the output and the state equations, when the dynamical evolution of the fault is completely unknown. In this study, the filter parameters are determined by minimizing an optimal upper bound for the covariance matrix of the state estimation error for all bounded and allowed uncertainties. The effectiveness of the proposed filters is demonstrated through numerical example that gives a robust and optimal estimation for the states variables and the unknown fault for stochastic uncertain systems.

articleTitle: Comparative study of some fractional PI controllers for first order plus time delay systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents a fractional PI controller design method satisfying both time-domain and frequency requirements. Also, the robustness to gain variation is treated. To show the importance of the obtained controller, a comparative study with an existing fractional PI controller tuned by F-MIGO method (Ms constrained integral gain optimization) is done. Some numerical example and an experimental test are given to show the efficiency of the proposed approche.

articleTitle: Robust LPV control applied to a personal pendulum vehicle
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Linear-Parameter-Varying theory has making a revolution during the last two decades to the study of nonlinear control and robust control, because they were taking into consideration the non-stationeries in the model and their uncertainties. In this article we suggest to exploit the LPV theory to design a robust gain-scheduled H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> controller applied to an Inverted Pendulum, specifically named Personal Pendulum Vehicle, which is a nonlinear system. The representation of both of the plant and the controller is a Linear-Fractional-Transformation (LFT) based LPV systems. The synthesis of the controller is achieved by scaling small-gain theorem and their tests are applied to the nonlinear model itself.

articleTitle: Decentralized model reference adaptive control for interconnected robotic systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of the decentralized adaptive control with model reference for a class of large-scale interconnected systems. The decentralized adaptive control law can guarantee the asymptotic stability of the overall interconnected system when some conditions are verified. The efficiency of the proposed control approach is highlighted by numerical simulation dealing with the decentralized stabilization of a robot manipulator.

articleTitle: Comparison between ultra-local model and auto-tuning PID controls strategies applied to the redundant manipulator robot for several inputs
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of an auto-tuning PID and an ultra-local model controls strategies applied to a redundant manipulator robot with a load on its endpoint. This system is dynamically modeled using finite element and Euler-Lagrange approaches. The proposed approach of ultra-local model control consists of estimating the ultra-local model parameter via an algebraic derivation approach. In order to validate its efficiency towards the flexibility's structure, the ultra-local model control is compared to auto-tuning PID controller using several inputs which are characterized by its optimal time and its smoothness. Numerical simulations show the simplicity and the robustness of the ultra-local model control compared to the auto-tuning PID control with respect to the flexibility's structure for several motions profiles.

articleTitle: A new chaotic encryption algorithm for WSN and implementation with sensors AS-XM1000
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In recent years the need for data communication security in wireless sensor network (WSN) has increased. The level of security varies from one domain to another and from one application to another depending on the type and importance of the data exchanged in the wireless sensors. In this paper we propose to conceive a chaotic encryption algorithm for WSN based on S-box and chaotic permutations. Comparisons other proposed algorithms are presented in this paper. The results of The evaluations and measurements of the proposed algorithm tests are done by using the TinyOS operating system, which makes it possible to manage the resources of the WSN. We will also present an implementation of the proposed algorithm on AS-XM1000 sensors. The proposed method is flexible; indeed the proposed encryption algorithm can be applied to messages of small size or large size as in the case of images.

articleTitle: The fault detection approach using bond graph model
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The fault diagnosis method in general involves detecting, identifying and locating the considered faults occurring in the dynamical system. We have tried in this study to show the exploitation of the Bond graph (BG) model with the fault signature matrix. The use of tools of the bond graph model of a process, allow us to detect the fault which are determined directly from the Diagnostic Bond Graph (DBG) and get the reason of a system dysfunction. Thereafter by bond graph, the localization procedure is based on the fault signature matrix generated by the Analytical Redundancy Relations (ARRs). In this paper, we present a statistical decision procedure to detect the operating mode. These tools allow us to detect the fault of a dynamic system dysfunction. Six tanks system is used to validate the approach in MATLAB/Simulink and to indicate the efficiency of the proposed fault detection procedure.

articleTitle: Design of 10.6 GHZ low phase noise LC-voltage controlled oscillator in 0.18μm CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: A low phase noise LC-voltage-controlled oscillator (LC-VCO) implemented in 0.18 μm CMOS technology is described in this paper dedicated to radio-frequency operation. The LC-VCO incorporates the differential NMOS cross-coupled pair as an active circuit to reduce the phase noise characteristic. The process to establish the oscillation frequency tuning is employing the LC tank core. Simulation results prove that the output frequency is 10.6 GHZ, an excellent phase noise (PN) which is -107.779 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from the 10.6 GHz carrier and the dissipated energy power is 9.8 Mw under 1.4 supply voltage.

articleTitle: Small size cubic antenna design for WSN
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work presents a new miniaturized 3-D cubic antenna used for wireless sensor network. The antenna is designed as a cube including a meander dipole antenna. An omnidirectional pattern is produced by this antenna in both E-plane for phi= 0° and H-plane for phi= 90°. The operating frequency is in the ISM band (2.45 GHz). The proposed antenna has dimensions of 1.25*1.12*1cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which characterized by the length dimension equal to λ/11. The overall antenna (Ka) is 0.44. The WSN has many problems and the major constraint is the energy consumption. In the radio communication unit the energy consumption is relatively high compared with other components. So it is necessary to design an antenna which improves the energy efficiency. The parameters considered of the proposed antenna are the return loss, bandwidth, and radiation pattern in terms of the directivity, the gain and efficiency. All results of the simulations were performed by the commercial software CST-MST.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of first order and second order discrete sliding mode control for non-minimum phase systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Discrete sliding mode control (DSMC) with the classical sliding function in input-output representation (I/O) is not feasible for non-minimum phase systems (NMPS), as the existence of unstable zero. To settle this issue, the first order DSMC (FODSMC) with the generalized sliding function (GSF) for NMPS is proposed in this paper. The trouble of the chattering phenomenon has been always the major problem of the FODSMC. As a solution, we propose a second order DSMC (SODSMC) via I/O model with GSF. The obtained control law is synthesized for NMPS. Simulation example is shown to illustrate the importance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: State feedback control against sensor faults for uncertain T-S fuzzy system: Descriptor approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work deals with fault estimation and robust state feedback control design for T-S fuzzy uncertain systems against sensor failures and subject to external disturbance with unmeasurable premise variables. The simultaneous estimation of faulty signal and system states is based on the descriptor approach which introduce the faults in the system having the property of auxiliary state. An observer based control strategy is developed based on the state estimates to stabilize the resulting closed-loop system using the technique of performance. The robust stability conditions are derived in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). The performances of the proposed control approach are demonstrated through numerical example.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of fractional order controller for induction machine control and comparative study between FOC PI & FOC FOPI
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The modeling and the control of the physical systems have experienced remarkable growing as soon as the fractional calculation appeared. In this research work, the Field Oriented Control FOC of the asynchronous machine is processed using fractional PI controllers firstly for current loops and on the other hand for speed loop. This type of control is recommended, since it accepts for their design additional degrees of freedom, to solve the problem of the complexity of this industrial system: the uncertainty of the electrical or mechanical parameters under the effect of the temperature and the improvement of the performances, robustness and stability of the system. The fractional order introduces a nonlinearity gives a better fit for the operation of the regulation. The FMINCON toolbox of Matlab is used to obtain the required values k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> and α.

articleTitle: Output regulation of nonlinear systems with FOPI controller based on singular perturbation technique
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this work an output regulation for first order nonlinear systems based on fractional PI controllers and singular perturbations technique is studied. The method objective is to guarantee desired performances in the presence of process parameters variations and perturbations. To obtain these performances, an optimization algorithm is utilized to determine the parameters of fractional PI controller. Then, the singular perturbations technique is used to evaluate the properties of the closed-loop system. A numerical example is presented to show the benefit of our method.

articleTitle: Blind equalization of OFDM systems based an optimal bounding ellipsoid under different channels
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a frequency recursive blind equalization algorithm of data in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system using a cyclic prefix. The proposed algorithm is based on a Set Membership identification methods. More precisely, it is based an Optimal Bounding Ellipsoid (OBE) algorithm. In this document, we consider the presence of bounded noise, of a single Input Single Output (SISO) fast fading channels such as Rayleigh and Rice channels. The numerical simulation shows that the proposed algorithm has good performance under different channels.

articleTitle: SIMO high frequency active universal current mode filter with independent control of pole frequency and quality factor
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: A high frequency universal current mode filter composed by three second generation current conveyor circuits (MOCCII), three active controlled resistances and two grounded active capacitors in this work. This circuit can simultaneously realize all filter responses without modifying the circuit configuration. This filter offers the following advantages: (i) pole frequency and quality factor can be tuned independently, (ii) all output terminals are high impedances which are good for cascadability to another circuits, (iii) low active and passive sensitivities. The workability of proposed filter has been verified by TSPICE simulation with 0.18 μm TSMC technology process parameters.

articleTitle: Hadoop based mining of distributed association rules from big data
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Data analysis techniques need to be improved to allow the processing of data. One of the most commonly used techniques is the Association Rule Mining (ARM). These rules are used to detect facts that often occur together within a dataset. Though several methods have been suggested for the extraction of association rules, problems arise when data becomes large. To overcome such issue, we propose, in this paper, an efficient approach for ARM based on MapReduce framework, adapted for processing large volumes of data. Furthermore, because real-life databases lead to huge number of rules including many redundant rules, our algorithm propose to mine a compact set of rules with no loss of information. The results of experiments tested on large real world datasets highlight the relevance of mined data.

articleTitle: High gain observer design for a class of MIMO nonlinear systems triangular with respect to an order
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a high-gain observer for a large class of MIMO nonlinear systems is considered. An order on the indices of the state variables is first introduced, which allows to characterize a large class of uniformly observable MIMO systems. This order is further used in order to design an observer whose underlying error exponentially converges toward zero. The approach is validated on simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis and robust LSDP control of a car suspension system with disturbance
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The present work discusses the modelling of a suspension (or detention) system for vehicles and the design of a robust controller using Loop Shaping Design Procedure approach for an active detention for a car model vis-a-vis disturbances dues to road unevenness.

articleTitle: Robust control of a DC-DC buck converter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This note is about the control of a DC-DC buck converter. Robust H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> methods are used to control the considered uncertain model. First, the uncertain model is introduced together with control specifications. Then, frequency direct synthesis is used to derive robust stabilizing controller for such system. Power systems toolbox is used for simulating the system. The obtained simulation results are given to show the effectiveness of the presented method.

articleTitle: Nonlinear modeling impedance electrochemical of PEM fuel cell
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This article deals with modeling the impedance of a PEM fuel cell. This work is based on experimental measurements proven by the actual stack. The fuel cell model describes the phenomena by a complex impedance specific to each cell. This model is given in the form of mathematical equations describing the non-linearity of the model. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy is requires studying the frequency behavior of the impedance model of the fuel cell by the Nyquist diagram. In this context, we have adopted the software “EIS Spectrum Analyzer”.

articleTitle: Impact of the modulation technique on overvoltage at the terminals of the induction machine fed by a voltage inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In industrial applications such as metallurgy, cement, and mining the asynchronous motor is usually installed far from the power supply. Thus, a long cable is needed to connect the variable speed drive to the asynchronous machine. Several studies had proven that the asynchronous motor thus powered will be solicited by a high voltage, which can reach twice the DC bus voltage. This paper presents two practical solutions for overvoltage mitigation. The first solution is based on choosing the most appropriate modulation technical for overvoltage reduction. The second one is frequently used in industry and it is based on interposing a filter between the inverter and the machine.

articleTitle: A methodology for thermal modelling and predictive control for building heating systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper handles the problem of a building heating. The used control strategy is the predictive control. Therefor a model describing the building with the thermal components such as a heat pump, a thermal solar connector and a storage tank is established and radiated in simulation. Than the control algorithm is tested. Simulation results are provided to illustrate the efficiency of such approach.

articleTitle: Early depth partitioning determination algorithm for SHVC encoding standard
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: SHVC standard is referred as the scalable extension of the high efficiency video coding HEVC standard. SHVC encoder adopts a quad-tree based structure allowing the use of block partitioning that fit better with the image characteristics. This technique may achieve a higher coding efficiency. However, it induces a significant computational complexity in the encoding process. In order to speed up the SHVC encoder an early depth partitioning determination algorithm is proposed in this paper. The proposed method is based on statistical observations and depends on the quantization parameter value as well as the frame type. The proposed method may achieve up to 17% time reduction for Enhancement layer processing (EL) with a tolerable loss in PSNR and a slight increase of the bit rate.

articleTitle: Implementation of remote control for time delay systems based on adaptive and internal model approaches
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work focus on practical implementation of remote control. Adaptive and internal model control (IMC) strategies have been adopted. Thus, the adaptive auto-adjustable controller is based on pole placement control method and the hierarchical identification strategy. Bluetooth has been used as wireless communication protocol. Practical results for two processes, first order system with variable time delay and fluid level control process, show satisfactory results of the application.

articleTitle: A new gases identification method based on noise spectroscopy using metal-oxide gas sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Electronic nose is a system, which can be used to identify the nature of gases using a sensors array. In this paper, we propose to present an electronic nose (E-nose) based on noise spectroscopy of metal-oxide (MOX) gas sensor response. After measuring the power density spectrum (PDS) of the gas sensor noise generated when the sensor is exposed to the tested gas, the obtained signal (PDS) is plotted and computed in order to extract a new feature that will be considered as a gas signature and used to identify the gas. The data array composed of eight measures (four different concentrations for nitrogen dioxide and ozone) and three variables (three sensors) has been inserted into principal component analysis (PCA) process. Results indicate that successful classifications have been gotten in the discrimination of two sort of gas using support vector machine (SVM) which shows 100% of success rate. The result of data analysis demonstrates that the E-nose technology combined with noise spectroscopy could be perfectly applied to identify pollutant gases.

articleTitle: H_/H∞ observer design for nonlinear T-S fuzzy systems subject to sensor and actuator faults
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, the detection and estimation problem of sensor and actuator faults (SAF) for nonlinear systems represented by Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy models subject to an Unknown Bounded Disturbance (UBD) is investigated. Moreover, we focus on state estimation. For this, we propose a new observer design to simultaneously estimate state and SAF vectors. This observer not only lead to estimate the actuator fault, but also to improve the performance of fault estimation. To maximize the fault effects on the residual and minimize the disturbance effects, we consider the H_/H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> performances. For the stability, conditions are given in term of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). Finally, simulation results are afforded to prove the mentioned process efficiency.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of sensor grids in a building system using BRIDGE approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper aims at designing a diagnosis tool for detecting and localizing faults in a building system. A Bridge approach based diagnostic reasoning is used because it proves to be more relevant to provide the possible fault modes including multiple sensor faults. The efficiency of this method is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: A roadmap for SDN-based network management: Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan case
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Due to technological blast in hardware, software and communications systems, computing devices in multi forms (laptops, cell phones, tablets...) and vendors are spreading all over the globe connecting billions of users, and communicating massive amount of data daily, through the underlining networking infrastructures. University campus is no exception. Typical users of an educational campus network are students, faculty members, and the administrative staff. The increase number of mobile users, BYOD, social media applications, real-time video and audio communications, and mobile based services are some of the major challenges that put huge pressure and stress on the university campus network operators to manage and satisfy their customers. In this paper a software defined network (SDN) based design is proposed for managing Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan (ZUJ) network to overcome the emerging networking challenges. Current ZUJ network service is focusing on provisioning best effort connectivity. Our approach is this paper is to explore the primary challenges faced by the ZUJ network administrators, examine the limitations of the current solutions, and then propose an SDN design that will overcome the limitations of the current deployed network.

articleTitle: Study and design of a controlled oscillator for an embedded system to measure the complex impedance of PEM fuel cell
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: We present in this paper the study and the design of a voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) for an embedded system to diagnose the PEM fuel cell. Some problems related to fuel cells used in the electric vehicle field are the management of its efficiency and the lifetime of its membranes. To do this, the diagnosis using measuring the complex impedance is an important phase. It is based on the injection of a perturbation signal at the output of the PEM fuel cell, then we observe its behavior by measuring its impedance. The used measurement method is the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) using the load modulation technique, which is implemented in an embedded measurement system based on a microcontroller. This embedded system needs a controlled oscillator using a frequency spectrum range from 10 mHz to 15 kHz.
