With this larger frequency bandwidth swiped for measuring the PEM fuel cell complex impedance, this oscillator is a first in the impedance spectroscopy field.

articleTitle: Decentralized optimal control for nonlinear interconnected dynamical systems with fixed final time using SDRE approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to assure the decentralized horizon optimal control of interconnected non-linear systems with fixed final time based on the Decentralized Finite-State Dependent Riccati Equation (DF-SDRE). We have also developed a new sufficient condition to ensure the stability of the studied system using the Lyapunov theory. A simulation of this new control method on a numerical interconnected system demonstrated its efficiency and the sufficiency of the new stability condition.

articleTitle: Decentralized observer based control design of nonlinear polynomial interconnected systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this communication we expose a numerical approach to design a polynomial controlled nonlinear interconnected system augmented by its observer and to determine their sufficient LMI global stabilization conditions. The key of this work is the description of the nonlinear systems using the Kronecker product notations and the power of matrices properties which allow easy manipulations for the state description of polynomial systems. The stability study of the polynomial controlled system augmented by its observer is based on Lyapunov stability direct method. The simulation results are applied on a numerical example to check the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Structural and parametric identification of linear systems with delay or a slow initial onset
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper deals with the identification of linear systems developed on the Meixner-like basis. Two aspects will be considered, namely the identification of the structure of the model obtained (pole of the base) as well as the identification of its parameters (Fourier coefficients). It should be noted that the model structure is linear with respect to the Fourier coefficients while it is not with respect to the pole. So as to reduce the number of model coefficients, the optimum value of the pole is determined by the method of minimizing the Normalized Mean Square Error. Once the structure has been determined, the second step will be carried out in which the domain of the coefficients of the resulting model will be updated. Two domains have been addressed, namely the polytope and the ellipsoid. Also, the interval analysis method has been proposed in this article.

articleTitle: New study on the distribution of EM fields near the GSM cellular networks in the urban area of greater tunis
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, we studied the distribution of EM fields in the GSM-900 cellular network on sites in Greater Tunis. The method adopted to simulate the electrical radio propagation aspect of these sites is a known professional simulator PLANET-EV. The results we have found shows that the GSM network produced a high level of field in the vicinity of the base station, and can bother the subscriber's EM environment, and could be considered as a source of noise for other systems.

articleTitle: Development of control strategies in a wind energy conversion system based on PMSG
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents the control strategies and the modeling of two sets power converter, where one has been connected to the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) side and the other one, has been connected to the grid side. The right side converter is controlled by Field Oriented Control (FOC). The control of this system is achieved by using Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control for extracting the maximum power and proportional integral (PI) correctors to control the speed and the d and q-axis currents. The control algorithm of grid side is based on Direct Power Control (DPC) to ensure the injection of a pure active power in the grid. The proposed subsystems are simulated using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: The rotor-flux-oriented control of the induction machine used the multicarrier strategies for multilevel npc inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The rotor-flux-oriented control of the induction motor used the multicarrier strategies for the three-phase multilevel NPC inverter. It applies the PWM strategy of command making a difference between carriers superposition to create new PWM strategies. This work compares two commands of multilevel strategies based on PWM; the PDC-PWM strategies (Phases Disposition Carrier-Pulse Width Modulation) and the PSC-PWM strategies (Phases Shifted Carrier-Pulse Width Modulation).

articleTitle: Model-free control of LTI systems: An algebraic state estimation approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This manuscript is concerned with the robust stabilization of a class of Linear Time Invariant (LTI) systems. The considered controller is based on output derivatives estimation. For the state estimation, a non-asymptotic approach based on elementary algebraic manipulation will be used. This approach leads to specific formulate for the unmeasured states. The robust stability synthesis of the closed loop is studied via Lyapunov function approach leading to the system and the observer-based controller discretization. An example of a second order system is given to illustrate the effects of the sampled period and the estimator parameters.

articleTitle: Neutral system with variable time-delay: Stability analysis and diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The present paper proposes stability analysis and diagnosis methods for neutral systems with variable time delay. Stability condition depending on delay value, is proposed using the Lyapunov-Krasovskii approach for the neutral system with variable delay and robust control. A new unknown input observer is designed as a diagnosis approach with two new conditions to decoupling the effect of fault and disturbances in the residual comportment for the stabilized neutral system. Important conditions were introduced to guarantee the UIO application for the neutral system with variable time delay. Finally, a numerical example proves the effectiveness of obtained stability approach and the designed UIO applied for the neutral system with variable time delay achieves fault detection.

articleTitle: Adaptive state observer for time delay systems with uncertainties and delayed state perturbation
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper treats the design methodology of adaptive state observer for a category of linear time delay systems with unknown delayed state perturbations, parameter and structured uncertainties as well. Considered on Lyapunov stability theory and solved with linear matrix inequalities technique (LMIs), necessary and sufficient conditions of the existence of such observer are obtained to ensure the asymptotic convergence of estimation error to zero value. We propose a simple structure of the design of the linear adaptive observer which is the combination between a state observer and an adaptation law that estimates the unknown delayed state perturbation and the states of the system as well. Finally, we give simulation example to make sure that the proposed design methodology is feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Delayed sliding surface for time delay system
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In most existing SMC, for analyzing the time delay system using the conventionnel SMC, we will transform it to its regular form, taking account a restrictive assumption. In this paper, a novel sliding surface dependent on both the state and input vector is proposed, in order to remove the restrictive assumption. Furthermore, it can be improved the effectiveness of the proposed SMC by adding the delayed states. The sliding surface can be obtained, By constructing a suitable Lyapunov-Karsovskii Functional (LKF) and uses the most recent techniques such as Wirtinger-based integral and the reciprocally convex approach. A simulation example is studied to illustrates the advantages of this method.

articleTitle: Modeling and control of a photovoltaic generator connected to a medium voltage Tunisian feeder
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper studies the impact of photovoltaic energy injection into the grid. First, a 2kW photovoltaic emulator based on an inverter and a photovoltaic voltage-current look up table data is presented. The system is connected through a transformer to a medium voltage Tunisian feeder. Grid's real data were used to build a realistic model. Power, current and voltage measurements are presented and the influence of such energy installation on the grid is studied. Second, the impact of a 0.5 MW photovoltaic power injection on the same distributed line voltage is analyzed. Simulation results show in one side that the PV emulator reproduces different V-I curves and provides optimal power owing to the mppt strategy. In the other side, it confirms that the photovoltaic energy injection supports power needs and reduces voltage drop at extreme node. It also improves voltage stability and decreases lines losses in the case of high load level. Finally, it shows that in absence of power compensation, reactive power transit can be significant especially with low load level. This amount can be used for local voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Parametric and state estimation for nonlinear polynomial systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This manuscript deals with parametric and state estimation problem of discrete-time nonlinear polynomials systems. In this respect, the aim is to design a Recursive State and Parametric Estimation (RSPE) algorithm, based on least square principle, polynomial adjustable models and Kalman filter theory. Our simulation results show the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Steady-state analysis of a variable speed traction system using DFI-motor
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Variable Speed Traction System (VSTS) equipped with large asynchronous machines are emerging now in electric vehicles applications. This work deals with a conventional configuration of the VSTS which consists on a Doubly-Fed Induction Motor (DFI-Motor) supplied by two power-converters one for the stator windings and another for the rotor ones. It investigates the fundamental steady-state theory of the DFI-Motor and analyzes its behavior using MATLAB. Formulas for currents, active and reactive powers in the stator and rotor terminals as well as electromagnetic torque are deducted as a function of the rotor phasor voltage. The rotor injected voltage is controlled by varying the two parameters of its complex form which are: the magnitude and the internal angle. The simulation results show that proposed control strategy is correct and feasible.

articleTitle: An outlier detection/rejection method for single-trial EEG signals classification
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: We address the key issue of the presence of outliers and artifacts inherently present in various electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. Indeed, in almost all brain-computer interface (BCI) systems, EEG signals may contain artifacts and noisy components frequently caused by improper imagination or by a loss of concentration during the imagination process. In this paper, a method is firstly proposed to detect the outliers from training and as a second step to reject those artifacts and outliers on the basis of training. In particular, the method proposed can operate for all kind of EEG signals contaminated by noise; in addition to remove the need of human expertise. Experimental results conducted on BCI competition 2003 dataset III show significant improvement of performance accuracy compared with the standard classification scheme.

articleTitle: Comparative study of fuzzy logic peak power trackers for a photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: As the photovoltaic produced power is depending on weather conditions, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller are usually applied to extract the maximum amount of generated power. This work provides a review of MPPT controllers based on fuzzy logic concept. The studied system includes a PV panel, a DC-DC converter and a resistive load. The classical MPPT algorithms fail to track the maximum peak power point (MPP) accurately, so that fuzzy logic is introduced to reduce oscillations around the operating point as it can trace the maximum power for all the cases. Three fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLC) are developed using different types, Mamdani and Takagi-Sugeno (T-S), and different input and output signals. The proposed algorithms are tested under dissimilar atmospheric conditions and compared to a conventional MPPT technique, Perturb and Observe. FLCs provide quick reaction to the weather conditions variation and decreased fluctuations around the MPP.

articleTitle: A reduced-order unknown input observer scheme for a class of nonlinear fractional-order systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The issue of concepting reduced order continuous-time observers has been subject to several research works. Up to now, only very few papers have treated the specific one-sided Lipschitz class of systems with unknown inputs. Likewise, the literature contains very few works treating reduced order observers for fractional-order systems. Recently, a unifying attempt has been done to construct reduced order observers for one-sided Lipschitz fractional-order systems, but with no unknown inputs in the model. By the present paper, we design a reduced order observer for that same class of systems, taking into consideration the unknown inputs.

articleTitle: Statistical interference description in 4G mobile communications networks
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Routing multiple signals is a capital goal for an operator. For that, network's generations' architectures are continuously reviewed in order to overcome various encountered challenges. Efforts remain however limited despite notable introduced enhancements. Operators must guarantee sufficient protection for every terminal even when multiple signals are simultaneously routed. The offered quality in each case will be indicated to see how the solution becomes difficult when cell's size goes shorter. Unfortunately, we will show how various added signals appear jointly with those useful ones. These added and unwanted parts define interference and affect needed signals. Quality manifests a decrease when customers move from wide and clearer space to a narrower one. This situation characterizes particularly urban contexts i.e. cities. In response to these challenges, technicians try to enhance the established solutions giving a better Quality of Service (QoS). From one mobile network's generation to another, cell's radius becomes smaller. Recently, we hope to approach punctual sites as previewed in D2D communications. Operators look to provide their customers satisfaction. They aim mainly increasing the offered data rates. The aim of this paper is to verify that the received power in radio mobile communications follows Rayleigh distribution. The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section II will recall the data rate enhancements. Interference problem is described in second mobile network's generation up to fourth's one in section III. Section IV gives simulation results showing a perfect correspondence between theoretical and practiced approaches. Finally, the last section concludes the paper.

articleTitle: Improved mobile base station model for satisfying delay and energy constraints in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks are sometimes used for delay sensitive applications such that health monitoring and forest fire detection applications. In such applications, gathering sensory data does not consider only energy issues but also timeliness constraints because much delay can cause big damages. In this paper we make a tradeoff between energy conservation with the use of the well-known mobile sink technique and the respect of delay requirement. We formulate a new optimization problem using linear programming and perform many computational experiments on it.

articleTitle: Active fault tolerant control using bond graph formalism: The hydraulic system case study
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The present work deals with Fault Tolerant Control (FTC) problem which is a significant topic, nowadays, treated to accomplish industrial process safety and better yields especially for energetic systems. Thus, a Bond Graph (BG) model-based approach to synthesize an Active Fault Tolerant Control system (AFTC) has been suggested here. The proposed approach is developed using the output feedback control methodology and failure estimation to accommodate their effects referring to BG structural and causal properties to calculate controller gains. This allows an on-line adjustment for our controller parameters to guarantee closed loop stability and accuracy. The treated fault can be detected and identified through a graphical adaptive observer. To validate theoretical results and to show controller efficiency, an hydraulic system with two tanks has been studied.

articleTitle: Electric appliance type detection: Approach for estimating residential energy consumption
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Non-intrusive appliance load monitoring (NIALM) systems are essential to assess real-time energy consumption and provide accurate analysis of the area, device and use. By dividing the information obtained from the total consumption of electricity into individual devices, it may raise clients' understanding of the energy consumed by the house, develops the economic behavior of energy and provides a general energy oversight for residential buildings. NIALM systems are aimed to reduce our energy expenses while increasing our comfort. It can detect which devices are used by signaling the individual energy consumed by each. This may indicate behaviors, such as routine hours when no one is at home, or embarrassing or illegal behavior of residents. To solve this problem, several studies propose new monitoring strategies to reduce the waste of energy in buildings, but they present a significant computation time and a complexity of algorithms. In addition, they ignore the problem of energy estimation. This article proposes an NIALM approach based on elementary loads detection and device types classification. It shows the accuracy of the event classification for each device as well as the correctly assigned energies.

articleTitle: Multiple ultra wide band sources localization with time reversal technique using FDTD
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents a Time Reversal (TR) algorithm, applied to localize multiple targets in Ultra Wide Band (UWB) using Finite Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method. Based on some numerical simulations executed by the FDTD programs, it's shown the performance of the UWB-TR-FDTD proposed algorithm to detect multiple targets in homogeneous medium and also behind the wall. Among this research, the results illustrate and confirm the efficiency of the algorithm in radio-frequency sources detection both in the case of homogenous medium and through the wall.

articleTitle: A novel frictional force control of a wheeled robot
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper considers one of the most widespread problems in mobile robotics called the natural environmental constraint evolution of terrestrial mobile robots problems. The lands with severe slopes are among the unreachable areas by mobile robots. To overcome this critical problem, a particular architecture is proposed to help wheeled robots to maintain steady movement on acute slopes. The principle of this strategy is to act on the friction force that can compensate the tangential component of the weight that prevents the robot to be able to move in these severe lands. Therefore, a reduced model of the used motor is defined and introduced in the control loop of the friction force to reach adequate performances. Finally, real time experiments are accomplished to valid simulation results.

articleTitle: PI controller design for linear systems with delay or a slow initial onset
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The present work proposes a new method for synthesizing a PI control algorithm using Meixner-like model. The Meixner-like model is used to represent the linear system with delay or a slow initial onset. The optimization of the Normalized Mean Square Error is considered to estimate the optimal Meixner-like pole. The proposed control approach is tested on a numerical example.

articleTitle: Interval Type-2 Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy model based control design for nonlinear stochastic system
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper the problem of the fuzzy control nonlinear stochastic system is addressed. Firstly, an Interval Type-2 Takagi Sugeno fuzzy model, that represents an extended version of the Type-1 Takagi Sugeno fuzzy logic system, was proposed for the purpose of the description of the nonlinearity. Next, refereing to the parallel distributed compensation's concept (PDC), an Interval Type-2 fuzzy controller is developed. The design of the above controller is performed with a manner ensuring the closed loop stability. Stability conditions of the Interval Type-2 Takagi Sugeno fuzzy model based (IT2 TS FMB) control system are presented using the linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). In order to evaluate the performance of the suggested design method, simulation results performed on benchmark example are finally given.

articleTitle: A novel method for optimizing the ratio of image compression
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, a method for increasing the compression ratio, is presented. This method is sensitive to the smoothness of each block in the image, where, the criterion of smoothness is the standard deviation. For a certain level of smoothness, the block can be approximated and represented by only its spectral DC component. The resulted blocking artefacts, introduced during this compression process, can be enhanced by smoothing of the blocks boundaries. Two factors are affecting the compression ratio, The first is the smoothing factor (threshold) for standard deviation. The second is the used quantization table. Experimental results, using MATLAB, demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can optimize the trade-off between compression ratio and quality of image.

articleTitle: Immunity test of RF MEMS of non uniform test radiation techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This work presents the immunity test of radiation techniques in terms of near fields. The simulation results of the electromagnetic aspects of the proposed test are given by the commercial software Computer Simulation Technology Microwave Studio (CST-MWS) based on finite integration technique (FIT) method. The immunity test results are performed in the both states (OFF and ON switch) in the frequency range between 1 and 40 GHz. The treated parameters for this test are insertion loss, return loss, E fields and H fields. The simulation results of the immunity test for RF MEMS capacitive given in different position of the electric probe. The obtained results show that the immunity of the component is according to the wavelength λ, the frequency f, the position of electric probe and the state of the component.

articleTitle: Recovery of linear local models of a system
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to locate and recovery linear behaviors of a nonlinear system. For this, we have used an ART2 neural network algorithm to a clustering process. In the simulation stage we have considered a system with three linear comportments. All system behaviors are present in a data file which is used to achieve a validation clustering step. A comparative study with three classification algorithms is then made.

articleTitle: On the use of differentiator in sliding mode control of uncertain robot manipulator
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Control of manipulators is very crucial since their large propagation in many fields. This paper deals with a sliding mode approach for tracking control applied to a two-degree liberty manipulator as a nonlinear uncertain system. A robust differentiator is integrated with sliding mode control satisfying joint torques velocity estimation. The principal goals of this suggested method are to minimize sensors number and to ameliorate control performance. The results of simulation prove the differentiator robustness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Comparison of fuel consumption and emissions of two hybrid electric vehicle configurations
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Hybrid electric vehicles have investigated as an alternative form of transportation to minimize environment problems. They offer multiple advantages over conventional vehicles including, among others, decreased fuel consumption and reduced emissions of harmful greenhouse gasses. The objective of the present study is to compare fuel consumption and gas emissions of both parallel and series hybrid electric vehicles by means of an advanced vehicle simulator. These two chosen vehicle types share the same dimensions and have the same mass. The simulation results in city and highway driving cycles were reported and compared and discussed. Finally, some conclusions were drawn and some perspectives of future work were outlined.

articleTitle: Inter-turn short-circuit fault detection in the vectorial control PMSM drive
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents an inter-turn short-circuit of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) operating under the direct field oriented control. A new simple method to detect stator windings incipient damage and to classify the fault severities is proposed for PMSM. This strategy is based on a fault indicator defined as the sum's square of the stator currents values in phases a, b and c. To show the effectiveness of the proposed fault indicator some simulation results using LabVIEW are presented.

articleTitle: Deep MLP for systems modeling
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: It is difficult to model complex systems such as greenhouses using classical methods. To drive the internel parameters of this system we have chosen deep learning neural network technique. We have used a feed forward neural network for direct modeling of the process. We have compared three structures of neural networks and the simulation results proved the efficiency of the structure to two hidden layers for modeling the process.

articleTitle: H2 — H∞ static output feedback control for vehicle chassis stability with input saturation
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper describes an output feedback control with input constraints for a lateral and roll vehicle dynamics model in critical motions. The variation of the road adhesion coefficient is considered. To this, a T-S disturbed model is proposed and a static output feedback control is designed with assuming that the lateral velocity and the roll angle are unavailable for measurement. The designed controller not only ensures the stability of the resulting closed loop system but also the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> - H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> performances. Based on Lyaponov theory, the controller gains are obtained by solving a set of Linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) constraints. The proposed techniques have been evaluated using a bicycle model with four degrees of freedom using Matlab software.

articleTitle: Neuro — Fuzzy methods coupled to operational PID, to improve the flight parameters of a drone
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The Neuro-Fuzzy (NF) technique makes it possible to exploit the learning capabilities of neural networks on the one hand and the reasoning capabilities of fuzzy logic on the other hand. It is extremely convenient because it incorporates all the benefits of both algorithms and makes the whole system more robust. We apprehend the simulation of our system by the PID regulation real test accompanied by NF algorithm. We find that the operational PID control coupled by ANFIS is more robust and gives better results compared to PID regulation alone. The simulation results generated by Matlab / Simulink, which provides a complete set of tools. Flight parameters UAVmodel with ANFIS controller coupled PID is simulated to verify the capability of the system. Finally, the results are validated by F450's drone.

articleTitle: Multi-robot navigation in an environment containing moving target based on hybrid approach
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this paper, we are interested in the problem of multi robots navigation system using the strategy of navigation in formation. The robots try to join a set of virtual targets forming a specific shape around the dynamic target. For this purpose, a hybrid architecture control is proposed, combining fuzzy system as a reactive method and sliding mode control as a deliberative approach. Simulation results show the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Security issues in controller area networks in automobiles
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: Modern vehicles may contain a considerable number of ECUs (Electronic Control Units) which are connected through various means of communication, with the CAN (Controller Area Network) protocol being the most widely used. However, several vulnerabilities such as the lack of authentication and the lack of data encryption have been pointed out by several authors, which ultimately render vehicles unsafe to their users and surroundings. Moreover, the lack of security in modern automobiles has been studied and analyzed by other researchers as well as several reports about modern car hacking have (already) been published. The contribution of this work aimed to analyze and test the level of security and how resilient is the CAN protocol by taking a BMW E90 (3-series) instrument cluster as a sample for a proof of concept study. This investigation was carried out by building and developing a rogue device using cheap commercially available components while being connected to the same CAN-Bus as a man in the middle device in order to send spoofed messages to the instrument cluster.

articleTitle: Face detection and tracking system with block-matching, meanshift and camshift algorithms and Kalman filter
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The aims of this paper is to propose a novel method for solving problem face detection and tracking system based in four algorithms: block-matching (BMA), Meanshift, Camshift and Kalman filter. Firstly, BMA is applied to the different sequential test as a preprocessing stage to detect faces. Then, the face tracking system are with three modules: Meanshift, Camshift and Kalman filter. This scheme gives a better face detection and tracking. Our work increases the performance and other criteria values in the embedded system. The human is more and more interested in producing intelligence which is one of the most impressive features of natures. Researchers are trying to make intelligent machine that have various capabilities. Building a machine or robot is probably one of the most challenging problems which humans are trying to solve. Recently, many projects have started with the purpose of learning machines to track some particular objects. One of the most challenging applications in computer vision is tracking objects efficiently in video sequence. Though progress has been accomplished, the best algorithms are far from reaching the speed and the performance of system. Object or multi-object tracking (face, human, car, etc.) is a fundamental problem that merits particular attention, since it is the key to solve a number of computer vision applications.

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence-based control for torque ripple minimization in switched reluctance motor drives
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: In this research paper, a control mechanism proposed to obtain the speed control of Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) with reduction of torque ripple employing a meta-heuristic design is presented. The proposed control scheme employees hysteresis current controller for the inner loop and fuzzy logic speed controller for the outer loop at the same time the control of commutation angles turn-on(Θon), turn-off (Θoff) and demagnetizing(Θd) angles for the three phases, 6/4 pole switched reluctance machine. The problem is to find optimal values of scaling factors of fuzzy logic controller structure of speed controller, hysteresis bandwidth for current loop controller along with the Θon, Θoff angles and demagnetizing angle are treated like a multi-objective decision making problem with the objective to minimize the Integral Squared Error (ISE) for both torque and speed ripple. In this work, a new approach based on the Ant Colony optimization (ACO) meta-heuristic technique is applied to find the adequate operating parameters values of SR motor. Comparison between conventional and intelligent controllers is achieved, firstly using PI-controller which tuned manually for a previous study, secondly using fuzzy logic controller which tuned by ACO technique.

articleTitle: A low-overhead fault tolerant technique for TSV-based interconnects in 3D-IC systems
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: 3D-Network-on-Chips (3D-NoCs) are considered as one of the most advanced and auspicious communication methodologies for future IC designs by exploiting the benefits of Network-on-Chips (NoCs) and 3D-Integrated Circuits (3D-ICs). However, their reliability still remains a major problem due to the vulnerability of Through Silicon Vias (TSVs). Because most of the existing techniques rely on correcting the TSV defects by using redundancy or employing routing algorithms, the TSV-cluster defect tolerances encounter costly area and power consumption penalties. In order to solve this issue, we propose a highly scalable and low-overhead TSV management for 3D-NoC systems where the TSVs of a router can be utilized by its neighbors and an adaptive online algorithm is also performed to assist. With this proposal, we aim to maintain a graceful performance for 3D-NoCs without the need for redundant links or employing routing algorithms.

articleTitle: ECG signal parameters extraction using intelligent adaptive algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: The investigation of standard electrocardiogram signal is one of the basic routine tests, which are used in order to detect or predict various cardiac disorders by interpreting the information provided by the Electrocardiogram. ECG signals are generally affected by various noises such as power line interference and the baseline drift that can be degraded necessary information. The extraction of pure cardio logical indices from noisy measurements has been one of the major concerns of biomedical signal processing. Therefore, an efficient process with good performance (accuracy, speed) must be essential. This signal first undergoes a preprocessing stage for noise cancellation followed by a P-QRS-T waves detection stage. The first stage deals with denoising ECG signal using different types of wavelets. The performances of algorithms applied for biomedical data processing are evaluated and compared in terms of basic parameters such as Mean Square Error (MSE), and Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR). In terms of P-QRS-T waves detection, we have described a comparative study between Pan Tompkins and wavelet algorithms. After applying two P-QRS-T waves detection algorithm on various recordings of MIT-BIH database, it is necessary to validate their efficiency. articleTitle: Comparative study between three control technics for photovoltaic voltage regulation
publicationTitle: 2017 18th International Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (STA)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between three control technics for photovoltaic PV voltage regulation. A current fed CF synchronous buck converter was used as power stage interfaced to the photovoltaic generator PVG in order to charge a battery connected to its output terminals. The PV voltage regulation was achieved using linear classic control technics and using a constant frequency sliding mode control CFCMS technic. The classic linear methods are simulated with a PID controller designed using poles placement technic and with a PI controller designed using the K-factor methodology. For the SMC, a new sliding surface was proposed. The different methods were detailed with all design steps serving as a tutorial for photovoltaic voltage control. These technics were simulated and tested using Matlab Simulink.
